name: Macro Maker
description: Works out a way through the level with measured 2.2 physics, checks it by playing it, and writes the result out as a macro.

effort.name: Effort
effort.description: How much searching each attempt is allowed. Quick is a first look, Thorough keeps a wide beam alive and takes minutes on a long level. Custom uses the three numbers below.

beam-width.name: Beam Width
beam-width.description: How many part-routes stay alive at each physics step. Wider finds tighter routes and costs proportionally more. Only used on Custom effort.

flight-interval.name: Flying Decision Spacing
flight-interval.description: In ship, wave, UFO and swing the search only considers changing the button every this many physics steps. One is frame perfect and slow. Only used on Custom effort.

search-seconds.name: Seconds Per Attempt
search-seconds.description: Wall clock ceiling on one search. The search runs on its own thread, so the game keeps drawing while it thinks. Only used on Custom effort.

flying-limits.name: Flying Modes Are Held In A Band
flying-limits.description: Whether a ship, UFO, wave or swing is stopped by an invisible ceiling and floor either side of the portal that started it. Off, because play says there is no such thing; turn it on if you find a level where the game does hold a flying mode in.

verify.name: Play It Back To Check
verify.description: A route is found in the simulator, which is measured but is not the game. Fast replays it through the real game as quickly as the machine allows; Watch replays it at normal speed so you can see it; Off writes the macro without checking it.

verify-rounds.name: Retries After A Death
verify-rounds.description: When the real game kills a route the simulator was happy with, that spot is marked as expensive and the level is searched again. This is how many times that is allowed to happen before it keeps the best route it has.

verify-ms.name: Checking Time Per Frame
verify-ms.description: How many milliseconds of fast replay to run each drawn frame. Higher checks the route sooner and makes the window feel frozen while it does.

write-gdr2.name: GDR2 (.gdr2)
write-gdr2.description: The binary format Eclipse Menu and the newer bots read. This is the one to leave on.

send-to-eclipse.name: Put It In Eclipse Menu's List
send-to-eclipse.description: Also drop the .gdr2 straight into Eclipse Menu's own replays folder, so it shows up in its macro list with nothing to move by hand.

frame-offset.name: Macro Frame Offset
frame-offset.description: Shifts every frame number written into a macro. Macros are timed off the game's own level clock, which should line up with whatever bot plays them; if yours presses consistently early, raise this, and if it presses late, lower it. 240 is one second.

write-gdr.name: GDReplayFormat (.gdr.json)
write-gdr.description: The older JSON shape. Some bots still read it; Eclipse Menu does not.

write-plain.name: Plain JSON
write-plain.description: Our own shape: every button change with the clock spelled out. Handy for reading, and for converting to a format nothing else here writes.

extra-folder.name: Also Copy Macros To
extra-folder.description: A folder to drop a second copy of every macro in, so it lands where your bot already looks. Leave empty to write only to this mod's own folder.

save-partial.name: Write Unfinished Routes Too
save-partial.description: Keep the macro even when the route only gets part way. It still plays up to where it got, which is usually the point of looking.

auto-play.name: Play The Macro When It Is Done
auto-play.description: Replay the finished route at normal speed once everything is written.

show-overlay.name: Show What The Simulator Sees
show-overlay.description: Draws the level the way the simulator was given it, straight over the real one: red boxes are what it thinks will kill you, blue what it thinks is solid, yellow the route it planned and cyan the path the game actually took, with the player's own box in white. Off by default because it is a diagnostic, not decoration.

show-hud.name: Show The Panel
show-hud.description: The readout with what it is doing and how far the best route gets.

key-make.name: Make A Macro For This Level

debug-log.name: Extra Logging
debug-log.description: Write what the level looked like to the simulator, and what each search round did, to the Geode log.
